issues.title: [Bug]: var-inferred function type loses its parameter defaults
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible arguments for function call
  --> 1788.bal:14:16
   |
14 |     io:println(g(1));
   |                ^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.edge_case_reason: Needs a function-type descriptor with a defaultable parameter, obtained via a record field and inferred with var.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `g(1)` rejected with SEMANTIC_ERROR 'incompatible arguments for function call'. Spec check (clean-context): var infers static type F; §6.15 uses the defaults from the function's static type descriptor, so the program is valid and prints 3 twice. Valid program rejected -> frontend (type inference for var drops param defaults). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: a call statement to a `never`-returning function is treated as completing normally
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: variable may not be initialized
  --> 1785.bal:14:12
   |
14 |     return x;
   |            ^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
// ----
error: stop
        at stop(1785b.bal:3)
           main(1785b.bal:6)
issues.edge_case_reason: Calling a never-returning helper (e.g. a fail/abort function) in a branch is ordinary code.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: false 'variable may not be initialized' for the definite-assignment case; the reachability variant compiles and panics at runtime instead of an 'unreachable code' error. Spec check: §7.4.3 reachability uses the static type; a never call cannot complete normally (§7.17 wording 'is possible' is a spec typo for 'not possible'). Flow analysis (CFG) bug -> frontend. Related but not duplicates: #1539, #1540.

issues.title: [Bug]: calling a resource method that has an unnamed path parameter panics with "too many arguments"
issues.output:
error: too many arguments
        at main(1784.bal:11)
issues.edge_case_reason: Unnamed resource path parameters (`[int]` with no name) are a rarely used construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: runtime panic 'too many arguments' (a Ballerina error, not a Go crash). --dump-bir shows `resource get n/[int] C.$resource$get$0() -> string` with no parameter, whereas the named form `[int i]` produces `$resource$get$0(int)` and runs correctly; the caller passes the path argument in both. BIR is wrong for the source -> frontend (BIR gen omits unnamed path params). Spec check: §5.6.3.5 makes the param name optional; program valid, prints 'anon'. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML template accepts a literal `]]>` in element text
issues.edge_case_reason: A literal `]]>` inside XML template text is an edge-case value.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: compiles and prints `x]]>y`. Spec check: §6.6.2 parses the template with XML `content`; XML 1.0 CharData excludes `]]>`, so a compile error is required. Missing diagnostic -> frontend. Related (other missing XML well-formedness checks), not duplicates: #1587, #1588.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML template accepts a processing instruction with the reserved target `xml`
issues.edge_case_reason: XML declaration / reserved `xml` PI target inside an XML template is an unusual construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: both templates compile and print unchanged. Spec check: §6.6.2 uses XML `content` (no XMLDecl); PITarget excludes 'xml' in any case, so both lines must be compile errors. Missing diagnostic -> frontend. Related, not duplicates: #1587, #1588.

issues.edge_case_reason: Declaring a no-init variable of type `never` is a rarely used construct.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: both local `never x;` and module-level `final never x;` compile and then panic at runtime. Spec check: §7.11 and §8.7 say 'The type-descriptor must not be never' for no-init declarations. Missing diagnostic -> frontend. No duplicate found.
